title: F1 proponent: BERLIN + CLOCK as substitution + columnar key pair
hypothesis_summary: BERLIN (positions 64-69) and CLOCK (positions 70-74) are the two strongest disclosed plaintext anchors. The proponent reading is that they ALSO function as cipher keywords — one substitution, one columnar — under a Vig/Beau/varBeau substitution layer composed with a keyed columnar transposition. This is the simplest structurally honest reading of the disclosed-crib evidence under a hand-cipher hypothesis.

provenance_items.quote_or_summary: Disclosed plaintext span BERLIN at indices 64-69 (Sanborn 2010).
Disclosed plaintext span CLOCK at indices 70-74 (Sanborn 2014).
Tier-1 entries BERLIN, CLOCK, BERLINCLOCK in the project clue registry.

composition_templates.rationale: Two-keyword sub + keyed columnar. Simplest hand-cipher form compatible with both keywords as keys.
Beaufort sub + keyed columnar. Same role pairing under Beaufort arithmetic.

constraints: Both keywords must be tried in both substitution and columnar roles (i3 generator handles this).
Allowed keyword pool restricted to BERLIN and CLOCK only — no project defaults.
caveats: BERLIN/CLOCK are KNOWN plaintext spans. The pack tests whether they could ALSO function as keys — a structurally independent question. Tier-1 evidence on the spans does NOT translate to tier-1 evidence on a key role.
PROPONENT framing — the same evidence supports much weaker readings.
